2026-08-27: Root cause of the prior draft's 106-differing-halfword score was a mismodeled call, plus two smaller unrelated bugs in the first loop. `Func_08007304` is not a real function: 0x08007304 is the r8 slot of the fourteen-entry `_call_via_rN` indirect-call trampoline bundle at games/gs1/asm/080072e4.s (`bx rN; mov r8,r8`, 4 bytes/slot, at 0x080072e4 + 4*N for N=r0..sp; r8 is the 9th slot). r8 is never an argument-passing register on this compiler (arm_function_arg in alchemy-gcc/agscc/gcc/config/arm/arm.c stops at r3), so a 3-argument call to 'Func_08007304' can never legitimately compile to code that also loads a jump target into r8 -- the prior draft's memcpy-shaped direct-call model was impossible by construction. Traced the true call target directly in games/gs1/asm/080b9470.s: at 0x080b94f6 `ldr r1, [pc, #88]` resolves (pc=0x080b94fa, word-aligned to 0x080b94f8, +0x58) to the literal-pool word at 0x080b9550, which the .s file lists as `.4byte 0x03001388`; that value is then `mov r8, r1`-ed immediately before the inner for-loop (`.L6`) and reused for all three `bl Func_08007304` calls inside it, reloaded fresh once per outer do-while pass. 0x03001388 is the codebase's already-established IWRAM word-copy routine -- the exact same address, with the exact same `typedef void (*WordCopy)(void*, const void*, s32)` idiom, is already used this session in games/gs1/recon/en/main/080d1350.c and games/gs1/recon/en/main/080e7404.c (and as `WordCopyFn`/`WordCopy` variants in games/gs1/src/battle/effects/member_orbit/run.c and games/gs1/src/graphics/palette/update_phase_palette.c). Rewrote all three call sites as genuine indirect calls, `((WordCopy)0x03001388)(dest, src, 16)`, and removed the fictional `Func_08007304` prototype.

2026-08-27 (same pass), two more confirmed bugs found and fixed in the untouched first loop while investigating the above: (1) sign-extension -- the prior draft named `u16 encoded = entry->encoded_action;` ahead of the `Func_08077008` call, which both reordered the load *before* the call (reference loads owner_id, calls Func_08077008, and only then loads encoded_action via `ldrh`) and caused `(s8)(encoded >> 8)` to compile as `lsrs` (logical shift) instead of the reference's `lsls #16; asrs #24` arithmetic sign-extend sequence. Fixing this needed both: not naming `encoded_action` as a variable used before the call (inlining `entry->encoded_action` so the load lands after the call, matching reference load order and its `ldrh`), and giving the `(s8)` cast its own named `s8 group = (s8)(entry->encoded_action >> 8);` local so the compiler couldn't fold the sign-extend away (an anonymous, immediately-masked cast expression got optimized straight into a logical shift instead). (2) literal-pool mask constant -- the reference loads the `0x0f` command-nibble mask via `ldr r3, [pc, #52]` from the same literal pool holding the 10000 priority-boost constant, not via an immediate `movs r3, #15`; matching the codebase's established idiom (see games/gs1/recon/en/main/080b1bd0.c) required `extern u8 Value_0000000f;` plus `group & (s32)&Value_0000000f` in place of the plain `& 0x0f` literal. Together with the WordCopy fix these two brought the first loop and swap-address bookkeeping (r5/r6 cursors, branch offsets, load/compare sequences) to a near-perfect structural match; also renamed the two loops' shared `index` variable to separate `i`/`j` locals, which independently fixed a pre-existing r6/r7 register-letter swap across the whole function (106->96->80->78 differing halfwords across these fixes, cumulative).

2026-08-27 (same pass, residual not closed): differing_halfwords=78, wrong_instructions=60, candidate_bytes=228 (byte-length now exactly matches the reference's 228, unlike the prior draft's 232). Confirmed via ~10 direct A/B compiles that this spill is a stable RTL/register-allocation-level artifact, not a surface source-shape issue: identical result (78-80 diff, same spill pattern) regardless of whether the WordCopy pointer is (a) a named local re-declared each do-while pass, (b) three repeated inline casts at each call site, (c) hoisted the same way with only one of the three calls converted (still spills with just one indirect call present), (d) explicitly void*-cast at every argument, (e) given an explicit `struct BattleQueueEntry *t = &temporary;` alias, (f) combined with an explicit `struct BattleQueueEntry *base = entries;` alias for the parameter, or (g) with `temporary` declared at the if-block, for-loop, or do-while scope. A `prev = j - 1` local variant did lower raw differing_halfwords slightly (76) but at the cost of breaking the otherwise-perfect entries[j]/[j-1] address-cursor decrement pattern (the compiler stopped recognizing `b = a - 16` and recomputed both addresses from scratch each iteration), so it was rejected as a worse structural match despite the marginally lower score; the delivered candidate keeps the clean, fully-matching address/branch/load structure. This is the same class of GCC-2.96-era register-allocation rigidity documented at length in games/gs1/recon/en/main/080a8c2c.json's mechanism note for a different owner (there a local-alloc.c qty_compare tie-break; here a global-alloc-level four-slot overflow) -- not resolved by source reordering, not attempted via register-qualified locals or inline asm per project rules.
